title: Kirby Problem 1.47
exact_target: Determine the least complexity of a nonorientable surface bounded by a knot, and all possible complexities and normal Euler numbers.
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
For a smooth knot $K\subset\partial B^4$, consider compact, connected,
nonorientable smooth surfaces $F$ properly embedded in $B^4$ with boundary $K$.
Write $b_1(F)=\dim H_1(F;\mathbb Q)$ and define
\[
\gamma_4(K)=\min_F b_1(F).
\]
Here the competitors are nonorientable, including when $K$ also bounds an
orientable surface. The normal Euler number $e(F)\in\mathbb Z$ is the relative
Euler number of the normal bundle, evaluated with orientation local coefficients,
using the zero-linking boundary framing of $K$. It measures the obstruction to
extending that boundary normal section to a nowhere-zero normal section on $F$.

Determine $\gamma_4(K)$ and, more precisely, the geography set
\[
\mathcal G(K)=\{(e(F),b_1(F)):F\text{ as above}\}\subset\mathbb Z\times\mathbb N.
\]
The designated family question asks for these minimal first Betti numbers for
torus knots $T_{p,q}$, where $p,q$ are coprime integers of absolute value greater
than one and $T_{p,q}$ winds in the two directions on the standard torus in
$S^3$. A geography determination must specify exactly which pairs are realizable,
as well as obstructions to all excluded pairs.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Determine the least complexity of a nonorientable surface bounded by a knot, and all possible complexities and normal Euler numbers.
